source: A game where start at a stop with a train rail and every while or so there is a building with a gun inside. It has a 60 percent change of being a 1890s sawed off double barrel shotgun, 30 percent change of being a 1890s rifle, and a 10 pent chance of a 1890s bolt action rifle. There is a train that comes by every minute or so and you can hop on it. Some times you see a big green zombie. You can shoot it to hurt it and kill it.

image_prompt.text: Period buildings standing close to the track at intervals, each entered from outside and holding a gun
Narrow ground between the buildings and the embankment where an encounter is unavoidable
A train rail running the length of the map, with a small stop platform at the start
A train that travels the rail and passes the platform about once a minute, low enough to climb onto

layout_placement.text: Points near the buildings and alongside the track where the big green zombies appear, so the player can see them coming
One gun inside each building, rolled from a weighted table of period firearms
The player starts on the train stop platform at the head of the rail

notes: The PvE Shooter preset carries lane-network; the map is a rail line with buildings strung along it, so open-battlefield is used with the preset's option set.
collectible-loot was added on top of the preset because the weighted gun roll is the core of the prompt and the preset does not carry it.
The train is periodic moving geometry. Nothing in the handoff can express that it moves, how fast, or that the player rides it.

open_questions.ask: How far does the rail run - a handful of buildings, or a line long enough that the train ride matters?
Is there an end to the line, or is it an endless ride with zombies along the way?

theme: Late 1800s rural frontier - weathered timber buildings, dirt and scrub, period rail

coverage_missing.ask: How long is the rail line?
Is there a destination, or is it endless?
Straight period western, or something stranger given the green zombies?

answers.ask: How far does the rail run - a handful of buildings, or a line long enough that the train ride matters?
answers.answer: Make it a short line with a handful of buildings along it, so it stays small and playable.

answers.ask: Is there an end to the line, or is it an endless ride with zombies along the way?
answers.answer: Use an endless ride with zombies appearing along the way; the prompt does not call for an ending.
